repo_notes.content: skills is a set of agent skills (SKILL.md folders) tailored to the owner's projects: h0ffmann, piabrota and marola-dev. It is not a vendored collection. Each skill is written for those projects. README.md is the index. It is easy to fork: `just link` symlinks every skill into one flat folder that an agent reads.

Skills live in category folders: skills/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md. Categories: writing, research, dev-flow, nix, figures, web, notes, code, ouroboric. A skill name is unique across all categories and equals its folder name.

AGENTS.md holds the hard rules. Prefer its wording when documenting rules. The main ones: the whole repository is ASD-STE100; few links and low cognitive load; no duplicate skills; tailored, not vendored; never invent a fact; never weaken a check; the agent never merges or releases.

Token budget is a design goal. A description loads in every session, a body loads only when the skill is used, and a reference file loads only when the body names it. scripts/check.py enforces the budgets: 300 characters a description, 12000 in all, 150 lines a SKILL.md. Skills with `disable-model-invocation: true` add no description to the session and are run by name only.

Some files are copied as is and keep their text and language: the skills of piabrota/gramatico (ptbr-writer, ptbr, ptbr-routing, cientifico, retorica, bipr, figure) and archify (a git submodule in vendor/archify, MIT). check.py gives them warnings, not failures. Many of them are in Brazilian Portuguese.
skills/ouroboric borrows ideas from the ouroboric-dev organization (ideas by Bruno Valerio). No file of theirs is copied. Its README.md lists the public ouroboric-dev repositories.

The README drawing is the kanji 技 (waza, skill), drawn in pure Nix from hand-placed points: drawings/pen.nix (Catmull-Rom to cubic Bezier to Desmos expressions) and drawings/waza.nix. `just drawing` writes docs/drawings/waza.svg and waza.desmos.json. The flake has one input, nixpkgs-lib. There is no CI: `just check` runs every check locally.
Write this DeepWiki in English, in short and plain sentences. Cite the SKILL.md of a skill for its behaviour.
